title: Permutation Sequence
summary: Given a set of numbers from 1 to n, find the k-th unique permutation of these numbers in lexicographical order.
statement: Given a set of numbers from 1 to n, find the k-th unique permutation of these numbers in lexicographical order.
constraints: Return the kth lexicographically ordered permutation of digits 1 through n as a string. k is one-indexed.
hints: Permutations sharing the first digit form equal-size factorial blocks.
Convert k to a zero-based rank, select its block, then repeat within that block.
Divide rank by (remaining-1)! to choose an unused digit; retain the remainder for the suffix.
Remove each chosen digit so it cannot be selected twice.
editorial: Convert to zero-based rank. With r digits remaining, each next-digit choice contributes (r−1)! consecutive permutations. The quotient selects the next digit from the sorted unused list, while the remainder is the rank within that block. Remove the selected digit and continue. List removal gives O(n²) total time, far less than enumerating n! strings. The independent oracle does enumerate permutations lazily and selects the kth entry.

tests.explanation: The order begins 123,132,213, so the third permutation is 213.
Each first-digit block has 3!=6 permutations. The ninth lies in the 2-prefix block and is 2314.
